Peter and Christine welcome their rivals to The Angel Inn in Wangford, Suffolk, where they get the ball rolling with a round of golf. But their self-service breakfast is a disappointment.
Lesley takes a laid-back approach to hosting at Moaps Farm B&B in Danehill, East Sussex. Her guests are blown away by the views, but there's chaos at breakfast.
Sisters Lorraine and Amanda host at their vineyard and restaurant B&B, Jabajak, in Carmarthenshire. Their guests are given the runaround as they attempt to herd sheep.
Les and his head chef Lesz hope to dazzle their rivals at The Clarendon Royal Hotel in Gravesend, Kent. Their guests are impressed by the food, but the leaky teapots let them down.
It's the final day of the competition and the B&Bers meet for one last time to settle some scores and find out how much they've been paid, before the winner is announced.
Salon owner Hannah hopes to tickle her guests' taste buds with a menu of flavoursome sensations, on a night filled with laughter and revelations.
Funeral director and BMX fanatic Simon plans to get his guests' hearts racing with some so-called 'man' food and a display by one of the UK's leading BMX riders.
Pascale prepares a Vietnamese menu full of flavour and colour, but Hannah discovers an unwanted guest in her main course..
Fourth host Nick prepares a menu that represents his personality - big, bold and brash. But will his venison impress.
Estate agent Ajay pulls out all the stops on her nautical-themed evening, with a seafood spread and a boat trip around Torquay harbour. But will she sail to victory.
The week kicks off at The George Inn in Barton-upon-Humber. Pete's hoping his cosy décor and quality cuisine will give him the edge, but the roadside location isn't up some guests' street.
At Cross Farm Cottages in Holmfirth, Claire reckons she can pip her rivals to the post. But Pete and Alex get antsy about the Artex, while Malaya has a firm opinion about his mattress.
At the New Valron Hotel in Blackpool, Malaya hopes that the seaside setting will blow his rivals out of the water. But a problem with the pipes sends the scores down the tubes..
Phil and Maria hope that their swish sense of style will impress their guests at The Spinney Homestay in Warwickshire. On a pedalo trip, the rivalry revs up with some raucous racing.
The B&Bers meet to settle some scores and find out who's won. Dirty discoveries and sleep issues are on the agenda, and one payment in particular leaves Phil and Maria out in the cold.
While freestyling in Virginia's Appalachian Mountains, Mike and Frank come across a hideaway packed with history, including mementos from a bluegrass legend.

d: Baby meerkat Junior is struggling to get enough food. Red panda Nima's new mate, Koda, chases her up a tree. And a shy penguin isn't socialising with his colony.

t: George Clarke's Amazing Homes on Wheels

Lizzie and Paul love the seaside town of Paphos on Cyprus's west coast. Can Ben Hillman find them the perfect holiday home for the whole family, including their 10 grandkids, for £125k.
Penny wants to move to the Spanish sunshine permanently and run her business from a new home in Málaga. Can Laura Hamilton find her the perfect place for her budget of £120,000.
Running enthusiasts Mark and Sally dream of owning a home in Greece's eastern Peloponnese. Will any of Jasmine Harman's options for their £200k get their hearts racing.
Lisa and Neil have holidayed on Menorca for decades. They love the lifestyle, scenery and climate and want to buy their own holiday home there. Jasmine Harman shows them what £250k can buy.
Retirees Clover and Mark want to find a new home in one of the stunning villages of Axarquía in Andalucía. Danni Menzies lines up five superb villas for their budget of £300,000.

Beauty school teacher Ashleigh serves up sophisticated grub with a side order of hearts and love.
Part-time farmer Stephen invites his guests to an evening on his farm, complete with a drinks reception in the stables and rustic home-cooked cuisine.
Prison transport officer Tina's sophisticated French menu includes salmon crêpes and posh peas, with expectations high after her criticisms earlier in the week.
IT manager David hosts a French evening, but can he keep Ashleigh and Tina away from each other's throats.
Helen and her daughter Lauren begin the competition at North Kingsfield Holiday Cottages in Yorkshire. But the bathrooms are showered with criticism and the lack of mirrors reflects badly.
At Crackin' View Guest House in Northumberland, Steve and Maria reckon their rivals will be blown away by their... cracking view. But there's a bangers clanger at breakfast.
Ali and his pal Serge host the third visit of the week, at the Domo Boutique Hotel in Birmingham. Helen's dazzled by the décor, but trouble brews over a caffeine conundrum.
At The Crown Inn in Norfolk, Lisa and Neil hope that their historic setting will bag them the B&B crown. But there are 'paneful' observations about the windows and a lorry-load of noise.

t: Find It, Fix It, Flog It
d: In Gloucestershire, Simon O'Brien and Henry Cole upcycle a horse yoke, a hay trailer and a fertiliser funnel.
Marianne and her housekeeper Fran welcome their rivals to Langsmeade House in Oxfordshire, where their quirky hosting and 1920s knick-knacks are a hit, but there's a surprise at breakfast.
Natasha and Dai host at the Stratford House guest house in Stratford-upon-Avon, but the family-friendly vibe doesn't gel with all their guests.
Michael and his mum Lorna host at Edmund House in Deal, Kent. One guest is less than thrilled by the 'no-frills' experience, and others don't fancy the activity: competitive dog grooming.
Entrepreneur Mark hosts at the Five Bells Pub in Berkshire. But his guests don't all share his passion for beer - and is he too honest for his own good.
The B&Bers meet for one last time to discover how much they've been paid, settle some scores and find out who's won.
Model, journalist and poet Azzi hosts in a Moroccan marquee in her garden... on a freezing winter's night. And her guests give her food an equally frosty reception.
Plucky plumber Steve Capel has an accident while preparing his favourite dish - an African roulade of ostrich, kudu and springbok - and his injury leads to carnage.
Former wedding planner Zae hopes to woo his guests with the attention to detail in his wedding-themed menu. But things don't go exactly as planned.
Events organiser Emma has her work cut out with her Italian menu - because she's never cooked a three-course meal in her life.
Jane is feeling the pressure, as she's out of practice hosting dinner parties. Can she get back into the swing of things with an adventurous menu and fancy dress.
The competition begins at NightSky Glamping in Abersoch, run by Angie and her daughter Caitlin. The guests love the hot tubs and views, but one of them admits that they hate camping.
Visit two is to Johnny Dough's Restaurant with Rooms in Conwy, North Wales. After a boat trip, host Morgan reveals his surprising past. Will his efforts produce good scores in the feedback.
We're off to the Peak District for the week's third visit, at The Royal Oak, run by Kadir. But two sets of guests experience some mouldy misery in their bathrooms.
The last visit of the week is to The Dovecote Inn in Nottinghamshire, run by Sam and Sophie. Can their cracking continental turn things around after an underwhelming day out.
On payment day, cutlery quibbles, grout gripes and breakfast bombshells are debated, before the payments are revealed and the winner is announced.

d: Kirstie and Phil are in Royal Wootton Bassett with Matt and Lucia, whose home is creaking at the seams. Can Phil's alternatives rival Kirstie's new layout plans.

d: A 47-year-old disabled woman is found dead with her throat cut. There are suspects but no hard evidence. But then the case takes a major twist.
